description: Build multi-species frontend architecture: species index page, individual species profile pages, updated globe with all species locations, and navigation between species
steps: Update index.html to transform the species section from a single tiger profile into a species gallery/index showing all 10 species as glass cards. Each card shows: common name, scientific name, IUCN status badge, ecosystem tag, and a brief hook sentence. Cards link to individual species pages. Keep the existing hero, globe, concept, and vision sections. Add schema.org JSON-LD structured data in the head for the site (WebSite, Organization schemas).

Create individual species HTML pages at species/{slug}.html (e.g., species/tiger.html, species/snow-leopard.html, etc.) - these should be full rich profile pages. Each page includes: (a) a hero header with species name, scientific name, and IUCN status, (b) taxonomy section from GBIF data, (c) habitat & range section, (d) media appearances section showing films/documentaries from OMDb data, (e) threats & conservation section, (f) cultural significance section, (g) navigation to other species. Use the same liquid glass design language. Include JSON-LD structured data (schema.org Species/Thing markup). Add proper semantic HTML (article, header, nav, section, aside) for LLM readability.

Create src/species-page.js - JavaScript module for species profile pages that: loads the species JSON data from /data/{slug}.json via fetch, populates the page dynamically, initializes GSAP scroll animations for the panels, and handles the species navigation. Include a loading state and error handling.

Create src/species-gallery.js - JavaScript module for the species gallery on the index page that: imports the species registry, renders the species cards grid with filtering by ecosystem, adds hover/focus glass effects matching the concept cards pattern, and handles click navigation to species pages.

Update src/globe.js to: (a) import the species registry, (b) replace the 5 hardcoded HOTSPOTS with dynamically generated markers from ALL species coordinates (should be 20-30+ markers total since species have multiple habitat locations), (c) color-code markers by species or ecosystem type, (d) add subtle tooltip on hover showing species name and location label, (e) keep the same atmospheric/aesthetic style but make it richer with more data points.
Update src/main.js to import and initialize the new species-gallery module instead of tiger-section, and handle routing logic for species pages vs index.
Update src/scroll-animations.js to add animations for the new species gallery section (staggered card reveals matching the existing concept card pattern).
Add proper meta tags and Open Graph tags to all pages for SEO. Ensure all pages have descriptive titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs.
Configure Vite (vite.config.js) to handle multi-page build: add species/*.html pages as additional entry points using rollupOptions.input so Vite builds them all.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds and produces dist/ with index.html and species/*.html pages
Index page shows a gallery of 10 species cards with the glass design language
Each species page loads its data from the corresponding JSON file in /data/
Globe shows markers for all species locations (20+ markers), not just 5
All pages include JSON-LD structured data
All pages use semantic HTML elements
Vite config correctly builds all HTML pages as a multi-page app
Navigation works between index and species pages
verification: Run npm run build and confirm dist/ contains index.html and species/*.html files
Check that dist/data/ contains all species JSON files (copied from public/)
Verify the built HTML files reference correct asset paths with the /species-on-screen/ base
findings: Build succeeds. dist/ output contains index.html, 10 species/*.html files, and 10 data/*.json files. Asset paths correctly use /species-on-screen/ base. Globe now has 31 markers from all species coordinates. The chunk size warning for globe-*.js (535KB, Three.js) is expected and non-breaking. tiger-section.js left in place (unused but not deleted per feature instructions).
